What a /23 means

A /23 gives 510 usable hosts, a good fit for a department, a floor or a medium branch office.

The prefix length is the number of leading bits that identify the network. A /23 uses 23 network bits and leaves 9 host bits, so the block contains 512 addresses. Usable hosts: 2(32−23) − 2 = 512 − 2 = 510.

Configuration examples

Cisco IOS

interface Vlan10
 ip address 172.16.0.1 255.255.254.0
!
access-list 10 permit 172.16.0.0 0.0.1.255

Juniper Junos

set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 172.16.0.1/23

Linux

ip addr add 172.16.0.1/23 dev eth0

Addresses shown are examples from private or documentation space. Replace them with your own plan.

FAQ

How many usable hosts are in a /23?

510. A /23 has 512 addresses; the first is the network address and the last is the broadcast address, so 510 are usable.

What is the subnet mask for /23?

255.255.254.0. The wildcard mask, used in ACLs and OSPF network statements, is 0.0.1.255.
